findings.title: Light/dark branches swapped for embedded-post username link color
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the first argument (light theme) should preserve the original 30%, with 70% as the new dark-theme value. As written, the values are inverted, so on light themes this username link changes from 30% to 70% lightness (much fainter than intended, hurting readability), which is a visual regression unrelated to the dark-theme goal.

findings.title: Light/dark branches swapped for .custom-message-length color
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the branches are swapped relative to the convention used everywhere else in this PR (original value in the light branch, new value in the dark branch). The desktop equivalent (`desktop/modal.scss`) correctly uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. On mobile light themes this text now renders at 30% lightness instead of 70%, making it far darker than before and inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should keep the original 20% (the desktop counterpart in `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). On mobile light themes, topic-map headings now render noticeably lighter than before, and mobile/desktop render the same element with different colors.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should preserve the original 30% (compare `.user-small .name` in `common/base/user.scss`, which correctly became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`). This silently lightens group member names on light themes beyond the intent of the change.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same mistake as in desktop/user.scss: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light branch should retain the original 30% value (e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`); as written, light themes get a lighter name color than before.

findings.title: Missed scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) instance in categories badge-notification
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, the exact pattern this PR converts everywhere else (including the visually identical `.badge-notification` rule in `common/base/header.scss`, which was converted to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`). On dark themes this leftover produces an over-brightened color inconsistent with the rest of the converted badge notifications.
